tabular.section: Author-hosted abstract of Watkins and Dayan (1992), Q-learning
tabular.summary: The original result addresses discrete action values in controlled Markovian domains, with repeated sampling and other convergence assumptions. Motion or stochasticity is not a categorical prohibition; this does not promise practical learning speed or safety.

basics.section: States and Observations; Policies; Reward and Return; Value Functions
basics.summary: An observation can omit state information. Policies can be deterministic or stochastic. Parameters include weights and biases. Transition probabilities and rewards are separate objects; value functions represent expected returns.

taxonomy.section: Model-Free vs Model-Based RL; What to Learn
taxonomy.summary: Algorithm taxonomies overlap. A model can be supplied or learned. Policy optimization can also learn a critic. Q-learning derives action choices from learned action values.

dqn.summary: The example has one output per discrete action. Training selects the experienced action output, computes successor values without target gradients, masks true terminal successors, and softly updates a separate target network.
dqn.version: Page says last updated 2025-06-16; accessed 2026-10-19. No claim to execute this external tutorial.

paper.summary: The publisher identifies the work as simulation-based navigation with RGB/CNN DQN, inflated-robot reward and CLIK tracking. Online publication was 2024-10-07; the issue is February 2025. Full article was not accessed.
